case_name: Smritikana Bag vs Dilip Kumar Bag
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties took place in 1976. The respondent husband presented a petition for annulment of their marriage under Section 12 and in the alternative for dissolution of the said marriage under Section 13(1)(iii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Although the petition was presented before one year had elapsed since the date of marriage, the respondent did not make any application under the proviso to Section 14(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act for allowing him to present the said petition for dissolution of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: To dissolve a marriage under Section 13(1)(iii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, the Court must be satisfied that the respondent's mental disorder is of such a nature and intensity that it would not be reasonable to compel the petitioner to endure or suffer the same.
legal_principles.held: The Court ought to be satisfied that the respondent's mental disorder is of such a nature and of such intensity that it would not be reasonable to compel the petitioner to endure or suffer the same.
cited_cases: Smritikana Bag vs Dilip Kumar Bag, (1981) X SCC Y
use_in: divorce cases involving mental health issues

legal_principles.principle: To prove a respondent's mental disorder under Section 13(1)(iii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, the petitioner must show that the respondent has been incurably of unsound mind or suffering continuously or intermittently from mental disorder.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner would be required to prove that the respondent had been incurably of unsound mind. Alternatively, he ought to prove that the respondent to the petition under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act had been suffering continuously or intermittently from mental disorder
cited_cases: Smritikana Bag vs Dilip Kumar Bag, (1981) X SCC Y
use_in: divorce cases involving mental health issues

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decree dissolving the marriage was set aside, and the case was remanded to the trial court with directions to consider the respondent's application under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
